dual.observation: Multiplicative resonance techniques that score +1 on PAO (alignment) systematically score 0 or -1 on kappa (cancellation). Selberg FE symmetry scores 0 on both. GHK hybrid scores +1 only as the surface for a future kappa proof, not as a proof.
dual.random_multiplicative_ceiling: {-1,0,+1}/Steinhaus models predict random-walk cancellation kappa ~ J^{-1/2}, which N1 arithmetic shows is insufficient for the M1.2 joint window. So the 'natural' multiplicative randomness is on the wrong side of the kappa bar.

conclusions.resonance: Multiplicative resonance is the correct classical family for on-line strong Omega (SOC on-line) and supplies amplitude Omega for PAO, but does not prove PAO(c,delta) measure lock at fixed gamma*. Kronecker torus alignment is dual-hostile to kappa.
conclusions.selberg: Selberg FE symmetry locks conjugate structure (already used) but does not open Iso_H/DH/PAO. Classical Selberg/Levinson mollifiers are false friends for O-Moll (score -1). AFE is the design surface for a future true O-Moll (+1 infrastructure only). GHK hybrid is the correct surface for a kappa theorem (+1 infrastructure).
conclusions.one_liner: Resonance feeds on-line strong Omega and PAO amplitude half; Selberg symmetry is mostly neutral with mollifier false friends; dual PAO/kappa tension is reinforced; no gap tip closed.
